name: Supply Chain

claims.claim_text: Buying components through the manufacturer's authorised distribution channel rather than open marketplaces is the basic defence against out-of-tolerance and counterfeit parts; a designer relying on 0.1 percent resistors meeting their stated grade sources them from a named manufacturer through a franchised distributor.
claims.quote_verbatim: you get them from a, you know, from a source. They're actually made by Burns, who are a top quality, you know, manufacturer. Yeah. And buy from DigiKey so they're genuine.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Raw-material extraction is concentrated in a small number of countries, and a disruption at that level propagates downward through refiners, component makers and assemblers to the finished product.
claims.quote_verbatim: they all need raw raw materials from somewhere. So it all just kind of propagates down the line
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A component supplier's institutional form is itself a sourcing criterion: a purchaser designing a part into a product assesses whether the supplier can be relied on to keep supplying it, and treats a hobby-scale vendor as a supply risk regardless of the part's technical merit.
claims.quote_verbatim: How is my supply chain affected by that hobbyist company?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: BASIC, Chip companies & Robots - Pernicious Projects, Puppies in Peril

claims.claim_text: Unit price for the same commodity passive can differ by roughly two orders of magnitude between a small buyer ordering singles from a catalogue distributor and a high-volume manufacturer buying direct.
claims.quote_verbatim: I pay four cents for a capacitor
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A component manufacturer's own web store may accept and charge for an order without displaying stock status, disclosing a months-long backorder only afterwards; catalogue distributors that publish live stock figures avoid this failure and are the reason a part is often ordered through distribution rather than direct.
claims.quote_verbatim: they don't tell you if they've got stock or not, right? They just say, you know, press here to add to your shopping cart. Fine. And they take all your credit card details, et cetera. And then I get an email last night saying, oh, sorry, we don't have any. Won't have them until February.

claims.claim_text: Below roughly one thousand units the labour content of assembly is a small share of total cost, so the shorter feedback loop, faster design-build-test cycle and stronger intellectual-property position of local manufacture usually dominate; offshore manufacture becomes economically compelling from around five thousand units upward, where labour and factory markup scale with volume.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're building, let's say, less than 1,000 units, then potentially the labor is a lot less important than if you're building a very high volume
claims.speaker: Scott Miller
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Miller - Sudden SinoAmerican Synthesis

claims.claim_text: Contract factories earn on volume, so orders below roughly five thousand units struggle to obtain a factory's attention and priority.
claims.quote_verbatim: the factories are a lot less interested for units under 5,000 because they make all their money on volume
claims.speaker: Scott Miller
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Miller - Sudden SinoAmerican Synthesis

claims.claim_text: The principal sourcing advantage of the Pearl River Delta is density rather than labour cost: components and vendor capabilities of almost any kind can be found inside a single region, which shortens the search and the logistics for every line item.
claims.quote_verbatim: just a remarkably robust and diverse supply chain. So you can find almost anything you want in terms of components, in terms of vendor capability, all within, let's say, the Pearl River Delta
claims.speaker: Scott Miller
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Miller - Sudden SinoAmerican Synthesis

claims.claim_text: A regional manufacturing cluster is an accumulated stock of infrastructure, parts availability and equipment built over roughly two decades, so it cannot be replicated elsewhere on the timescale of a wage change.
claims.quote_verbatim: not instantly because the infrastructure is not there. They've built up this infrastructure over a lot, you know, over 20 years
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: DIP projects, OSHW & Trade Booths - Demonstrative DIP Dacrygelosis

claims.claim_text: Lead times vary by component class, and a well-planned production programme can absorb worst-case lead times of four months or more, around sixteen to eighteen weeks, without stopping the assembly line.
claims.quote_verbatim: some of our lead times do get to be fairly high. Um, you know, four months.
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: Relocating assembly away from a components cluster removes the ability to recover from a stock-out locally; where the market is nearby a stopped surface-mount line can be restarted by buying a reel the same day, and where it is not, the line waits for a shipment.
claims.quote_verbatim: the supply chain support just really still isn't there yeah right you can't just walk down the local markets and pick up a reel because your smt line is stopped because you ran out of that part
claims.speaker: Andrew Witte
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: For small orders of low-value parts, freight and per-supplier shipping charges can exceed the cost of the goods, so a regional reseller's economic function is consolidating multiple origins into one shipment rather than adding value to the parts themselves.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're not really providing value on the electronics front. We're providing value in consolidating shipping for people
claims.speaker: Marcus Schappi
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Marcus Schappi - Kit Ketch Kenophobia

claims.claim_text: Memory and other high-volume semiconductor output is allocated in periodic lots, and a customer large enough to commit an entire period's production can do so, leaving smaller buyers with nothing for that period regardless of price offered.
claims.quote_verbatim: here's our lot for the month
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: We're Sorry! But Apple Ain't! - Remorseless RAM Racketeering

claims.claim_text: A dominant buyer can induce a component supplier to fund additional capacity against a promised order and then demand a price reduction once the capacity exists, because the supplier's new capacity has no alternative customer; a twenty percent reduction demanded after a capacitor vendor expanded for an automotive customer is a recorded instance of the pattern.
claims.quote_verbatim: we need more capacity. And so the company would go build capacity for it, right? And they'd say, Oh, that's great. Thank you. We'll buy all your parts, but we need a 20% reduction or else we're going to go over next door.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: We're Sorry! But Apple Ain't! - Remorseless RAM Racketeering

claims.claim_text: Just-in-time inventory is defined by the deliberate decision not to hold stock, with parts arriving as they are consumed.
claims.quote_verbatim: just in time is just that your parts. You don't, the whole concept is in a nutshell, if I've got it right, is that, uh, you don't want to hold stock.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Spacing Out On Space - Dave's Dongle Designing

claims.claim_text: Kanban was developed for vertically integrated automotive manufacture, where the supplying operations sit inside the same company and can be scheduled directly; a buyer purchasing catalogue parts from an external distributor controls none of the upstream steps and cannot apply the method in the same form.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's a lot different though, because that's in your company
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Spacing Out On Space - Dave's Dongle Designing

claims.claim_text: Building a product on top of a finished development board converts that board into a purchased component and inherits its availability risk.
claims.quote_verbatim: these actually become supply chain issues in themselves of buying, buying the finished goods board
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Someone is watching...we think - Horme Hostility Hypochondriac

claims.claim_text: Where supply is short, distributors and vendors ration on expected volume and end use, so a buyer taking a thousand units into a product is served ahead of a reseller taking three hundred at a time.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you have someone that's willing to buy up stock of 1,000, they're probably going to get... You know, for putting it into a product, they're going to probably get priority over someone who's buying 300 at a time
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: B Plus Boards and D Minus Cities - Uneath Urban Ubication

claims.claim_text: A product assembled from surplus and open-market stock has no fixed bill of materials; two production months of the same low-cost device can contain substantially different parts, because sourcing follows whatever was cheapest and available at the time.
claims.quote_verbatim: I bet if you bought this, this phone two different months, it could have potentially entirely different parts of it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, IndieGoGo & Ignite - Jasperated Jimswinger Jobbery

claims.claim_text: Choosing a part that has no pin- and feature-compatible relatives within its family eliminates any second-source or substitution path, leaving the design dependent on that single part number.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's no compatible parts within the family, so you only can buy that one part. Like, you buy the unicorn part, and you can never swap it in.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A contract manufacturer's supply-chain function works towards continuity by ensuring commodity parts carry several qualified alternates in the design, so no jellybean line item is single-sourced.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're going to help optimize supply chain. And typically it's, uh, so that you have supply chain continuity. So you don't have a single source component, especially for easy jelly bean stuff. They make sure that you've got a, a large number of alternates that you can specify in the design.
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Single-sourced specialised components must be settled early in a development programme, because securing volume for them can require a supplier to stand up an assembly line or a new factory, which takes far longer than the design work it supports.
claims.quote_verbatim: you sort of need to nail down a lot of things early in the process, especially single sourced components that might be hard to find alternates for
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Manufacturing near a dense supplier base shortens engineering support loops: a component problem that a datasheet cannot resolve can typically be answered by a local manufacturer's representative attending in person within a day or two.
claims.quote_verbatim: there seems to be no issue that within one or two days cannot be solved by bringing in like a local manufacturer's representative
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: On a factory visit, tools and consumables are carried in hand luggage rather than checked, because checked baggage can be delayed or lost and resupplying locally from an electronics market costs half a day of travel and negotiation.
claims.quote_verbatim: always bring what you can carry onto the plane because checked luggage can go missing
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor lead time sets a hard floor on a project schedule that no amount of resource can compress, and dependent tasks must be sequenced behind it; eight weeks is a working minimum for a chip order.
claims.quote_verbatim: we know that there is no possible way that we're going to get a chip in less than eight weeks because, guess what? That silicon is still sand.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Don't Turn It On, Don't Take It Apart

claims.claim_text: Supplier names and bill-of-materials costing are commonly withheld from an otherwise open hardware release, on the basis that the sourcing arrangement rather than the schematic is the competitive asset.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't think you have to give the name of your suppliers for sure or the costing on your bomb. I think that kind of stuff is competitive advantage of the supply chain.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Don't Turn It On, Don't Take It Apart

claims.claim_text: Sourcing advantages that are hard to copy include volume pricing unavailable to smaller buyers and exclusivity agreements under which a vendor supplies a given part to only one customer.
claims.quote_verbatim: Maybe I have an agreement with a, a vendor that they'll only sell a certain part to me.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Don't Turn It On, Don't Take It Apart

claims.claim_text: Display and component makers do not transact directly with small buyers at repair-shop quantities, so the independent repair trade is supplied by the overrun between a contracted build quantity and the parts shipped against it.
claims.quote_verbatim: they probably have to make 15,000 machines today and they get 15,500 screens
claims.speaker: Louis Rossmann

claims.claim_text: A component substituted for a cost saving can match the datasheet headline specification and still fail at the actual operating point; coin cells substituted to save one cent each met their paper specification but failed after a single use at the design's current draw, discovered only 24 to 48 hours before deployment of 21,000 units.
claims.quote_verbatim: the specs while they were on paper the same um the at the current draw we were we were at it failed after the first use
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: A factory that already builds a product class holds the sourcing relationships and tooling for its inputs, so a variant of an existing product can be quoted and run at a few thousand units without new supply-chain work; the incremental effort is design change, not procurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: they already have a supply chain to buy like huge amounts of lithium batteries and, you know, motors that have exactly the right torque capacity. And they already have like the lines to do the molding
claims.speaker: Bunnie Huang

claims.claim_text: Where a factory already runs the product class, a credible forecast of a couple of thousand units is enough to have a line duplicated for a variant within days.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you really think someone will buy like a couple thousand, sure, we'll two-up the line tomorrow
claims.speaker: Bunnie Huang

claims.claim_text: Designing a complete third-party board into a product as a plugged-in module is a sourcing risk and stops being economical once volumes reach the thousands, at which point the same function is integrated onto the product's own board.
claims.quote_verbatim: that can be risky from a supply chain perspective
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Hardware programmes are built under several division-of-labour models: specifying the product and contracting an original design manufacturer to design and build it, joint development of schematics with the manufacturer, or completing the design in house and using the manufacturer only for layout and fabrication.
claims.quote_verbatim: There are companies that act more in a developing the specification and hiring out to an ODM to actually build all the equipment.
claims.speaker: Rick Altherr

claims.claim_text: Development boards are priced as marketing vehicles at lower margins than production hardware and are built to a forecast of engineering demand; a single customer designing them into a product can consume the entire year's build and deny the boards to their intended audience.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're just going to design 4,000 of these into our product. And then they go and buy out the supply chain.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A platform vendor's volume purchasing can put a complete board below the single-unit distributor price of its main chip; a Zynq-based board sold at 55 dollars against a single-piece device price of about 70 dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can't buy a zinc for less than 70 bucks on a single-ship basis
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Adding a new part to a component library carries a recurring cost beyond symbol and footprint creation, because the part must be checked and its sourcing vetted; where a company employs a part librarian, that role is also where supply-chain screening happens.
claims.quote_verbatim: entering another part obviously costs more time in terms of checking and also then usually you start steadying up your supply chain through that person as well
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunding readiness cannot be judged from a claim that all parts are purchasable; the substantive tests are whether suppliers are contracted, whether payment terms and cash flow can carry the build, and whether the stock counted on has been secured, since uncommitted distributor stock can be bought out by another customer at any time.
claims.quote_verbatim: have you lined up all your suppliers is your supply chain in place you know is your cash flow secure did you get good payment terms
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: National holiday periods in a manufacturing region suspend production and shipping and must be built into delivery schedules by buyers ordering into that region.
claims.quote_verbatim: I got hit by like, uh, the, what, the Chinese Labor Day
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: For a small hardware company, engaging a tier-one contract manufacturer is generally the wrong choice; a local box-build house where the company's engineers can stand on the floor bringing up boards and designing test fixtures produces a working production process, because production competence is acquired by doing it rather than by delegating it.
claims.quote_verbatim: in most cases, that's a very bad decision for a small company to use a large, you know, tier one CM
claims.speaker: Ben Einstein

claims.claim_text: Supply chain, tooling and inventory management are the slowest-changing parts of hardware development and change far more slowly than component technology; they are constraints to be operated within rather than problems to be designed away.
claims.quote_verbatim: the sort of infrastructure, the supply chain management, the tooling, the inventory management, all that stuff. Uh, those are these big, heavy, slow things
claims.speaker: Ben Einstein

claims.claim_text: Crowdfunded hardware projects more often fail on execution than on concept, and the failures cluster in timelines, quality and supplier selection, where the founders had no prior exposure to the process.
claims.quote_verbatim: whether it's timelines or quality or, you know, bad suppliers or whatever
claims.speaker: Ben Einstein

claims.claim_text: A sole supplier of a technology to a defence customer can be required to standardise it and license it to competitors, so that the customer is not dependent on a single source.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're a sole supplier and you have a DOD customer, what they're going to do is require you to standardize it and, uh, license it to your competitors
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: In a company large enough to buy components by the reel and to employ supply-chain specialists, part selection is governed by the approved and stocked list, and a designer's freedom to substitute a preferred part at layout is correspondingly small.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have a supply chain expert in your company, there is very little chance that you get to tweak it on the PCB
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Chinese contract manufacture tends to be vertically integrated, with surface-mount assembly, injection moulding, mould making, final assembly, test and packaging under one roof, while United States and European manufacture is typically horizontal and requires the buyer to assemble several specialist vendors into a working chain.
claims.quote_verbatim: China tends to be very vertically integrated in that you'll have the, uh, SMT, uh, injection molding, maybe even mold making final assembly test packaging all under one roof
claims.speaker: Scott Miller

claims.claim_text: A horizontal supplier base costs more effort to assemble because there is no single accountable vendor, but a maintained database of which factories work well together and which already hold payment terms with each other converts that effort into reusable routing knowledge.
claims.quote_verbatim: it takes a lot more effort to put together your supply chain because it's not, you know, one throat to choke or one, one stop
claims.speaker: Scott Miller

claims.claim_text: Some semiconductor vendors appoint a single authorised volume distributor even where their parts are also listed by broad-line catalogue distributors; Xilinx volume business ran through Avnet, partly to simplify export compliance.
claims.quote_verbatim: Avnet is really only like authorized volume distributor for their parts. Um, and part of that has to do with export compliance
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The gap between single-piece and volume price is steepest for parts that turn over slowly in distribution, because the distributor's holding cost is spread over few sales; FPGAs with single-piece catalogue prices around 150 dollars are the standard example.
claims.quote_verbatim: the steepness of that, of the single piece price curve is, it's a little steeper on FPGAs for some reason
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Buying a module from a vendor who purchases the underlying silicon in volume gives a low-volume customer access to pricing they could not obtain themselves.
claims.quote_verbatim: customers get access to then your higher, you know, higher volume pricing with a Xilinx
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Sustaining engineering owns supply stability alongside field-failure root cause, because keeping a released product buildable is a continuing engineering task rather than a one-time procurement act.
claims.quote_verbatim: It also includes a lot more work like making sure your supply chain is stable.
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: A customer's purchase volume determines the commercial terms and the level of engineering support obtainable from chip vendors, and rising volume opens access to vendors who would not previously engage.
claims.quote_verbatim: as we got to the point where we were selling more and more products, we were able to get better and better deals out of a lot of our chip vendors and better and better support
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: A stopped production line at a contract manufacturer is the worst operational outcome for a hardware company, because the idle line accrues cost every day while producing no revenue; it justifies dispatching an engineer immediately regardless of distance.
claims.quote_verbatim: every day your line is sitting idle, it's costing you money and it's not making you any money
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: Recovery from a manufacturing-region shutdown is vendor-specific rather than regional; during the 2020 disruption some board fabricators resumed normal delivery while others quoted eight-week lead times.
claims.quote_verbatim: Oh, I can't get manufacturing. They're telling me eight weeks.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A stoppage at a component factory does not appear at the buyer immediately, because pipeline and distributor inventory continues to ship; the shortage surfaces weeks or months later when that inventory drains.
claims.quote_verbatim: if people aren't making parts at the, you know, the capacitor factory, that's not going to hit for a couple of weeks yet, but that could end up hitting later on
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Commissioning a custom integrated circuit can be justified purely as supply mitigation: a company dependent on a sole-sourced chip initiated its own design to remove that dependency, with the decision made by comparing the design investment against the exposure.
claims.quote_verbatim: they wanted to replace it for supply chain reliability because they only had the sole source and they didn't want to be dependent on it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Fabless Chip Design with Mohamed Kassem

claims.claim_text: Just-in-time supply optimises working capital at the cost of resilience, and a local buffer stock is the counterweight; short disruptions of only a few weeks produced effects that persisted long afterwards.
claims.quote_verbatim: Everyone loves just in time until you realize that kind of blows up
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Under allocation a supplier serves its largest committed customers first, and an order for ten thousand units is deprioritised behind million-unit accounts irrespective of the smaller buyer's willingness to pay.
claims.quote_verbatim: Hey, we'd like to buy 10,000. Like we can't deliver our million unit. Like, please leave us alone. Back of the line, please.
claims.speaker: Brandon Gilles
claims.episode_title: Depth and AI with Brandon Gilles and Brian Weinstein

claims.claim_text: During the 2021 shortage a critical part could be out of stock worldwide with a quoted lead time of 35 weeks, leaving redesign around an alternative part as the only practical response, since replicating an integrated function such as a boost converter in discrete form is not viable.
claims.quote_verbatim: And it's out in the entire world. And there's a 35-week lead time.

claims.claim_text: Scarcity induces purchasing agents to order more than they need to protect against being caught short, which inflates the apparent demand signal that suppliers plan against and leaves an inventory overhang once production catches up.
claims.quote_verbatim: then there's overbuying and it's just, so I think what's going to happen is in, you know, whenever the supply chain actually catches up, I think we're going to see a lot of extra chips because they're just all overbuying
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A supplier whose output is concentrated on one customer inherits that customer's demand swings directly; suppliers whose business was around ninety percent automotive shut down when the vehicle factories stopped ordering.
claims.quote_verbatim: then suppliers shut down because they're not getting orders from the auto factory and that was their 90% of their business
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Component suppliers whose parts are in demand triage inquiries by order size, and a vendor able to sell 50,000 units elsewhere will decline to engage with a 3,000-unit buyer.
claims.quote_verbatim: can you order 50,000 of these things? And we're like, no, we can, we can order 3000
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: A product spanning two industries inherits both of their supply chains and their incompatible ordering cadences: consumer electronics runs annual cycles with a handful of SKUs, while fashion runs quarterly seasons with twenty or more, and each side's factories treat the other's order pattern as unworkable.
claims.quote_verbatim: electronics yearly cycles, right? Like typically around, around early, early fall, you launch you once a year cycles. Fashion is quarterly
claims.episode_title: Firmware Deployment and Troubleshooting with Akbar Dhanaliwala

claims.claim_text: High-volume semiconductor procurement runs roughly six months ahead of production, so the order book behaves like a six-month first-in-first-out buffer and a buyer's place in it is set half a year before the parts are needed.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's a very, like a six month long FIFO buffer.

claims.claim_text: The 2020 to 2022 semiconductor shortage began with mass order cancellation rather than production failure: when demand was expected to collapse, large buyers cancelled the orders already placed six months out, their capacity was reallocated, and the cancelled buyers could not regain their place when demand returned.
claims.quote_verbatim: as soon as COVID started happening, all these companies suddenly went, holy crap, nobody's going to be buying a thing. And they shut down and they canceled all their orders.

claims.claim_text: Part identity is not stable across the supply chain: corporate splits, mergers and acquisitions leave the same physical component listed under two distinct entries, and a component management system must track subsequent part merges to keep one canonical identity.
claims.quote_verbatim: you will have two different parts in the supply chain, which are actually the same part. So there are part merges
claims.speaker: Jan Rychter

claims.claim_text: In 2020 parts remained obtainable from stock already sitting in distribution and in customers' hands even though factories had stopped producing them; that residual stock took until 2021 to drain, which is why the shortage was felt a year after its cause.
claims.quote_verbatim: The factories were not making the parts, but there were still a lot left in the supply chain. And then I think it took 2021 for them to actually dry up.
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: At the peak of the shortage distributor promise dates ran more than a year out, and designs were repeatedly revised, in one case to an eighth board revision, purely to accept whichever microcontroller could be obtained.
claims.quote_verbatim: microcontrollers are on their eighth rev of a board recently, the same board just revved to try and make, just to try and use anything that's in this
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: A placed order at a quoted lead time is not an allocation guarantee; a documented case had a component on a 28-week lead cancelled by the supplier in the 28th week after a larger buyer paid more, with no production shortfall involved.
claims.quote_verbatim: he had a component that was on a 28 week lead
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Individual hoarding propagates a shortage rather than solving it: a designer who redesigns onto an available part and then buys several reels of it removes that stock from distribution and pushes the same problem onto the next buyer who had planned around it.
claims.quote_verbatim: maybe there was stock of that one part before my friend bought it out. But now whoever was planning on that stock being in distribution has just hit the same problem
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Mixed Signal Education with Philip Salmony

claims.claim_text: Buying ahead is the main defence against allocation, so access to capital rather than engineering skill determines who can weather a shortage; a company unable to fund a forward purchase of its critical parts has no equivalent option.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you don't have the financials to actually purchase a certain amount to fit your design or production needs, that's a, that what I've seen is a real problem
claims.speaker: Philip Salmony
claims.episode_title: Mixed Signal Education with Philip Salmony

claims.claim_text: A company with no established supplier relationships takes one to two years to bring each product to market, because every sourcing step must be built from scratch rather than reused.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's taking one to two years to make any product for us because we are so small and like don't have any established supply chain yet
claims.speaker: Simone Giertz

claims.claim_text: Prototyping with a certified radio module and moving to a chip-down implementation for production is a recognised path, taken for supply-chain reasons as well as cost; the reverse trade is that a pre-certified module buys back engineering and certification time that a small team may not have.
claims.quote_verbatim: for initial prototyping, we used a module, but we quickly went to building that ourselves for supply chain reasons
claims.speaker: Ariel Briner

claims.claim_text: Buying critical integrated circuits up to two years before the designs that will use them is a defensible response to scarcity, but it converts a supply risk into a cash-flow burden by tying up capital in parts for products that do not yet exist.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's been horrible from a cash situation to be, you know, buying parts for things that haven't been designed yet
claims.speaker: Ariel Briner

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor manufacturers are not the base of the chain; they depend in turn on wafers, process chemicals and energy, so an upstream disruption reaches a designer through several intermediate layers.
claims.quote_verbatim: we think they're the bottom of the supply chain, it's turtles all the way down
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Qualified second sources for raw materials reduce but do not remove country exposure: alternates exist for most materials, yet they carry volume and capability constraints and cannot supply everything a manufacturer would want if the primary source were cut off.
claims.quote_verbatim: the other sources, which we have qualified, you know, will have a lot of constraints on them. And we won't be able to get everything we want.
claims.speaker: Steve Sanghi
claims.episode_title: Steve Sanghi - Microchip CEO for 31 Years!

claims.claim_text: A semiconductor manufacturer reduced its country concentration by stage: owning no assembly or test plant in one country, performing under five percent of packaging and only two to three percent of wafer fabrication there, while remaining dependent on it for rare-earth and other raw materials.
claims.quote_verbatim: We probably do less than 5% of our packaging in China.
claims.speaker: Steve Sanghi
claims.episode_title: Steve Sanghi - Microchip CEO for 31 Years!

claims.claim_text: Absorbing discrete support functions into the main silicon reduces both bill-of-materials cost and the number of separate parts that must be sourced, so integration is a supply-chain simplification as well as a cost reduction.
claims.quote_verbatim: One is it lowers the cost in general. And it also makes your supply chain a bit simpler.
claims.speaker: James Adams
claims.episode_title: The RP1 and beyond with the Raspberry Pi Hardware team

claims.claim_text: A component change introduced by a supply-chain substitution after qualification can push a marginal on-chip regulator over the edge with no failure indication, only reduced efficiency; where a device has a known sensitive internal converter, feeding the core rail from an external regulator removes the exposure.
claims.quote_verbatim: If your supply chain. Changes. Or something like that. Happens. Then. You could be right on the edge. And you don't know it.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A buyer of assembled product sits several tiers from the disruption, so an event today may not reach their purchase price or availability for twelve to eighteen months, and inventory held at each tier, often around six months' worth, sets that delay.
claims.quote_verbatim: if there was like a thing that happened today, it probably wouldn't ripple through to you until you put an order in in like 12 to 18 months
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The North American automotive supply chain is distributed across national borders by process, with engine blocks cast in Canada and wiring harnesses built in Mexico, so tariff and border policy applies to a product several times before final assembly.
claims.quote_verbatim: engine blocks are made like up in Canada and like the wiring harnesses are done in Mexico
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Electronics assembly is the last step of a chain whose inputs are themselves imported, so relocating assembly under a tariff regime only shifts the tariff exposure upstream to bare boards, laminate, process chemistry and semiconductor inputs unless those tiers are built out at the same time.
claims.quote_verbatim: you really need a lot of these, uh, the, the supply chain to be built out like simultaneously
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: Consumer electronics has historically been produced through original design manufacturers who handle both design and manufacture at high volume, leaving the brand with software and marketing; rising tariffs have made that arrangement less durable and pushed such companies to evaluate domestic assembly.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's this general trend to, uh, to increasing tariffs, I would say in the U S
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: An effective sourcing method for a new product is to locate an existing product closely resembling the intended one and trace the factory that builds it, because that factory has demonstrated the capability, holds the tooling and team, and can usually modify the existing design to a new specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: find a product that's similar or almost exactly like what you want to build and then work your network until you find the factory that actually builds it
claims.speaker: Eric Migicovsky
claims.episode_title: Shiny New Pebble with Eric Migicovsky

claims.claim_text: Open hardware release gives a company adopting a board the option to take control of its own supply, because the design detail needed to build or re-source it is available.
claims.quote_verbatim: they have that opportunity to kind of take control over the supply chain. They can get the details
claims.speaker: Jason Kridner

claims.claim_text: Heavy electrical infrastructure carries lead times measured in years rather than weeks; large transformers ran to a three-year backlog, and a grid-scale battery installation was taken partly offline by a transformer failure while the battery itself was undamaged.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's like a three-year backlog on these transformers
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Logistics disruption is a measurable cause of infrastructure failure: of the recorded serious United States power outages in 2014, 77 followed severe weather, 66 followed physical attack, and 17 followed fuel shortages caused by supply problems such as rail congestion.
claims.quote_verbatim: in 2014, there were 77 serious power outages in the United States due to severe weather
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Scaling a design beyond prototype requires both a documented, reliable datasheet for each part and an understanding of how that part is supplied; a component with no dependable datasheet is treated as a liability rather than a cost saving.
claims.quote_verbatim: I would never use a part that didn't have a data sheet that I could rely on
claims.speaker: Zach Fredin

claims.claim_text: For a function whose dedicated part is obsolete, the alternatives are sourcing secondhand devices desoldered from scrap boards, whose provenance and condition are unknown, or re-engineering the function from currently available parts, typically with a higher component count.
claims.quote_verbatim: I have to go buy these parts on eBay secondhand that are desoldered from a board in China

claims.claim_text: Small differences in device selection multiply through production volume and margin; the roughly two-dollar premium for a gigabit rather than a 10/100 Ethernet PHY was decisive on a board competing at a 35-dollar price point.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like an extra $2 to make a gigabit at least. So, you know, multiply that by your profit margins
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: A Security Update with Michael Ossmann
